unresolved.topic: Meaning of the first number in decimal(n,m) and number(n,m)
unresolved.detail: The Items sheet headers are Length and Precision. For S0142 decimal types those two columns are empty; only the full type string is filled. Precision in the second parameter is enforced as a maximum number of digits after the decimal point. Whether the first parameter counts digits before the decimal point or total significant digits is not stated, so it is not a failing check.

The workbook type names are date, datetime and boolean, with no picture. Accepted forms are an assumption documented in the README: YYYYMMDD, YYYYMMDDHHMMSS, and a short boolean word list. Valid-set names referenced by S0142, whose members are not listed in this workbook: P/C Flag, Price Derivation Code, Quarter Hour Period, Run Type.

unresolved.topic: Delimiter, AAA header and ZZZ trailer
unresolved.detail: The S0142 blocks do not name a field separator or a file header or trailer. Pipes, an AAA file-type version and a ZZZ trailer are assumptions. AAA and ZZZ field lists are not validated. Worksheets in this file: 'Multiple', 'SO', 'BSCC Ltd', 'FAA', 'Stage 2', 'Internal', 'NGC ', 'SVAA', 'Items'.
Parentage is taken from the L1-L9 marks. The workbook does not say that siblings must appear in sheet order. Sibling order is not enforced.

unresolved.topic: Which layout a settlement date uses
unresolved.detail: v014 comments say the P444 fields are populated for post-P444 settlement dates. The workbook does not give that date, and it does not say which layout version a file of a given date must use. The parser reads the version from the file. It does not infer one from the settlement date.

Optional fields may be empty. The workbook does not say that the four characters NULL mean absent, and it does not say that an empty field means zero. Empty optional fields are loaded as SQL NULL. The token NULL is a bad value for a numeric type.

The workbook comment on N0388 says a null means the same value as Period BM Unit Total Accepted Bid Volume, and N0389 has a similar comment. That is not a deletion and not zero. This tool does not copy the other field into the empty one.

unresolved.topic: Cited omission rules that a single file cannot decide
unresolved.detail: Change-only omission, the II/RF full-set wording, the BO4 send condition, the incomplete BO7 sentence, and the missing D-run baseline are listed under omission_rules.not_enforced. They are not guessed.

omission_rules.source: IDD Part 2 V55.0 section 5.23, as cited by the project notes of 2026-10-02. No cell in the V43.0 workbook states these rules.

not_enforced.reason: MEL, MIL, FP2, BO2 and BO6 are cited as present on SF/R1/R2/R3 only when the data version changed relative to II, and on DF only when it changed relative to RF. The cited wording is that a change counts no matter what the value was. These records have no data-version field in the workbook, so a second file of values cannot show whether a record should have been omitted.

The cited section says S0142 is a full set on II and RF. The workbook still gives MEL, MIL, FP2, BO2 and BO6 a minimum cardinality of 0. A missing optional record on II or RF is not reported as a defect.
BO4 is cited as sent on a price change, a BO2 change, or a non-zero or NZ-flagged acceptance volume. The workbook has no NZ-flag data item, and one file cannot show that a price changed.
The cited section 5.23 sentence for BO7 is incomplete and gives no rule. BO7 is checked only against its workbook type, optionality and parent.
No baseline run is stated for S0142 run type D.

The cited section says Replacement Reserve items are sent on every run. The workbook gives those groups a minimum cardinality of 0 and comments that several are reported for post-TERRE settlement dates only. The workbook wins: absence is not a defect.
No I014 sign convention for cashflows or volumes is stated in the workbook or in the cited S0142 sections. Signs are stored as written and are not interpreted.
